target_customer: Data science teams in enterprises that need to deploy models into applications
problem: Data scientists built models in R and Python but had no easy way to deploy them as APIs or manage them for use by applications.
business_model: Enterprise software licences for ScienceOps and ScienceBox
product_category: Data science model deployment and management platform

founders.name: Austin Ogilvie
founders.background_notes: The YC page says he later founded Thoropass.

founders.name: Greg Lamp
founders.background_notes: No further background on the YC page.

exit.reason: Announced at the Alteryx Inspire conference on June 6, 2017; terms not disclosed in the announcement. Yhat technology became Alteryx Promote.

technical_complexity.rationale: Packaging R and Python models into scalable APIs with versioning and monitoring needed solid infrastructure engineering, but not research.

defensibility.rationale: Once models are deployed through a platform, switching is costly, but cloud vendors and open source tools could offer similar deployment features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Alteryx, an analytics vendor, bought Yhat in June 2017 and rebuilt it as Alteryx Promote.

market_need_then: In May 2015 Yhat had 14 customers and a team of 9, and its second seed was oversubscribed against a $1M target, suggesting early demand for model deployment.

branding.domain_note: Used yhat.com; acquisition of the domain was not found.

identity.logo: Not described in the sources found
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical; the YC page says the name is pronounced y-hat

brand_strength.rationale: A statistics in-joke name that needs explaining to non-statisticians, with no evidence found of brand pull or community beyond data scientists.

outcome_analysis: Yhat sold ScienceOps and ScienceBox to enterprise data science teams, reached 14 customers by mid 2015 and raised a $1.5M second seed. Alteryx acquired it in June 2017 and used the technology for Alteryx Promote. The deal price is disputed across sources, so the outcome is best read as a small, strategic exit into an analytics vendor with total funding of roughly $2.5M, not a venture-scale outcome.
notes: yhat.com did not resolve (DNS failure), likely retired after the acquisition. Competition left empty: a search for dated competitors returned only current docs and a 2017 article on Domino Data Lab. A $1M seed in September 2013 appears only in a startupintros aggregator snippet and is unverified. The acquisition price is disputed: $14.7M cash and stock per the Orange County Business Journal citing Alteryx's 10-K (not opened), about $5.0M in equity per a filing report, and $10.8M per an unreliable encyclopedia site; all unverified, so amount is null. Aggregator totals: $2.62M (CB Insights), $2.5M (Seedtable). Austin Ogilvie appears on a SuperDataScience episode about the name, but the page was blocked, so name origin is null. Founder education not found.
